threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you’re new when you stare at the bus timetable like it’s a novel. Locals have already grabbed the next one without blinking.
Caught a night bus home from Brixton last week. The driver was having a right laugh with a group of mates, singing along to whatever was on the radio. Never seen that before!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids making a full-on marketplace with just a table and some old toys in Richardplatz. Such creativity in the air.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find an old factory turned into a rave venue — the vibe is electric but the walls tell stories of a time long past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Someone from here knows to avoid the BART delays and will totally plan an evening around those 5 PM ‘overheating brakes’ announcements.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 today—packed, but the driver stopped to let a musician finish his song before moving. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals see them as extensions of our living rooms, bustling with real conversations.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they hesitate at the 'pancarta' signs in the plaça—like they’re deciding if it’s a festival or a protest.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus stops at the oddest places. The locals know it’s the only way to catch a ride on a rainy day.
Last night on the 333, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old school R&B. Even the driver was chuckling. Best entertainment I've had in ages!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a guy playing sax on the bus, and the whole car started clapping. That’s when I felt the real Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you’re in Friedrichshain when the local kebab shop doubles as a late-night gallery, showcasing artists while your döner is sizzling.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know to keep their head down during a BART delay; tourists act like it’s a night at the museum when the trains stop.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 30-Stockton handed a breadstick to a tourist. He said, 'Welcome to San Francisco!' Traffic stopped for a moment, but it felt like a warm hug.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but real locals treasure the quiet corners where kids play and neighbors chat over old-school cafés.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the overwhelming excitement over trying pa amb tomàquet for the first time at a local bar. Classic sign.
